title: Change Nucleus software and contracts
summary: Modify Nucleus code, protocol, storage, Codex compatibility, authentication, service lifecycle, or deployment using the required guarded procedure.
use_when: Nucleus implementation, public protocol, persistent state, harness compatibility, authentication, service lifecycle, or deployment behavior is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is only to inspect or recover the installed runtime.
The change belongs entirely to Todo, Annals, Weaver, or another requester domain.
The user has not authorized release publication or deployment.
outcome: A minimal Nucleus change with the correct compatibility, migration, requester, documentation, CI, canary, and recovery obligations satisfied.
effects: Modifies Nucleus source, tests, contracts, or operator documentation.
Depending on the selected playbook, may require coordinated requester changes, database migration, exact Codex inspection, or service cutover.
Release and deployment remain separate externally consequential actions.
authority: Nucleus owns its protocol, store, adapter, authentication lease, service packaging, and operator manual.
Requesters continue to own their domain contracts and must be changed only when the shared boundary requires it.
success: Every changed public or operational fact is reflected in the canonical operator manual and exact contract documentation.
The relevant generic and requester canaries prove the changed boundary after any deployment.
failure_and_recovery: Do not attempt binary-only rollback after an incompatible store migration.
Do not replace the proved Codex executable without adapter inspection and compatibility tests.
Preserve forward-only authentication separately from program or database rollback.
privacy: Development fixtures, logs, and backups may contain complete prompts, model output, tool traffic, or credentials and must remain private.
Canaries create real runtime and sometimes requester-domain records; choose and account for them deliberately.
steps: Run `nucleus manual` and classify the change as a routine patch, protocol/client change, store migration, exact Codex upgrade, requester contract change, or authentication/service change.
Apply the smallest change in the owning Nucleus component and update all exact contracts and operator facts affected by it.
Run the Nucleus product CI and any affected requester CI suites.
If deployment is authorized, quiesce the required requesters, preserve the required recovery material, deploy in compatible order, and run layered canaries.
checkpoints: The primary authority and every cross-system obligation are identified.
Public compatibility and persistent-state consequences are explicit.
Deployment and publication have not occurred without separate authorization.
adaptation: Follow the exact playbook in the installed version-matched manual because store, harness, and requester compatibility facts evolve.
Use daemon-first or coordinated cutover ordering according to the compatibility shape actually introduced.
stop_when: A required migration or credential decision lacks safe recovery authority.
An affected requester cannot be quiesced for an incompatible operation.
The exact candidate Codex behavior has not been inspected and proved.
does_not_authorize: Running `release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Changing requester-owned domain meaning merely for runtime convenience.
